I have been farming this land for fifty years. My body tells me things now that it did not at thirty. There are only two of us — my wife and I. We cannot do what a younger household can do. But I know this land. I know what it needs.

My 8 mu is split the way it has always been: 6 mu for wheat and maize in rotation, and 2 mu for cotton. I have thought about giving up the cotton many times. It is hard work, especially picking in September. But it brings cash. Without cotton money I feel uneasy. 2 mu I can manage. My son comes back sometimes to help.

**Wheat (6 mu, planted October):** I always use the improved varieties from the township supply station — the same ones I have used for years. I will apply compound fertilizer as base and urea at jointing. Three irrigations: before winter freeze, at jointing, at heading. That is what I have always done. My hands know this. Two sprays — one for aphids in spring, one for powdery mildew. I use the rotary tiller now, not the deep plough. My back cannot manage deep ploughing anymore.

**Maize (6 mu, planted June after wheat):** I buy hybrid seed. Everyone does now — yields are better. The village machine station broadcasts the seed directly after wheat harvest without tilling. I leave it to them. I apply fertilizer once at planting and once when the plant is knee-high. Two irrigations if rain is short. One spray for corn borer.

**Cotton (2 mu, planted April):** This is the hardest. I plant improved seed — same as last year. I fertilize three times through the season. I irrigate four times. Cotton needs more spraying: aphids early, bollworm through summer. I do four applications. My wife helps with topping the plants and picking. We take it slow.

I do not try to maximize yields. I try to have a manageable season and bring in enough to live comfortably.
